$comment: The single source of truth for WHICH agents run and WHEN they run. MVP_PLAN_V3.md §9 forbids running Architect, Validator and Reviewer after every minor edit; this file is that rule made mechanical. `pnpm oracle packet` and `pnpm lanes decide` both read it, so the routing policy has one definition instead of one per prompt.
$capabilitiesComment: Capabilities, not agent names. Each list is preference-ordered and resolved to the FIRST agent file that exists under .claude/agents/. That is how this repository tolerates two legitimate role shapes at once: MVP_PLAN_V3.md §21 merges running and adversarial testing into `validator`, while `runner.md` and `tester.md` split them. Resolving by capability means neither shape creates a second owner for the same responsibility. `execute` (Runner) is in no class chain: deterministic commands are run directly by the Coordinator or the Builder, and Runner is dispatched only when its activation condition fires.
$classesComment: Change class decides the agent chain, and the LIFECYCLE POINT decides when each link runs. `perPacket` runs once per work packet; `perWave` runs once at the wave gate, over the wave's combined diff; `perPhase` runs once at the phase gate; `conditional` runs only when its entry in activationConditions fires. The onFailure path is not a per-class list: an unclear reproduced failure routes to the `diagnosis` class (Diagnostician → Builder → revalidate), per activationConditions.diagnose. A capability listed nowhere for a class does not run for that class.

mechanical.rationale: Deterministic and non-behavioral — a rename, a config move, a doc correction. The deterministic checks decide it. Nothing here has an oracle to falsify, so no Validator, no Reviewer and no Tester unless explicitly triggered.

feature.rationale: Normal implementation against a settled contract. Review catches the coupling that tooling cannot express — once per wave, over the combined diff. Validator fires only when observable behavior changed (which usually means the class should have been `behavior`).

behavior.rationale: Externally visible behavior, assertions, fixtures or the test oracle changed. One Validator per wave over the combined diff — this is where a green that lies gets written. Reviewer and Tester run at the phase gate: Tester is expensive independent falsification and is never per packet (tester.md states it; this file enforces it).

contract.rationale: Wire schema, shared interface, migration, or another shared write surface. Everything downstream inherits the mistake, so the contract is validated and reviewed per node, BEFORE the next lane builds on it. Architect fires only when the interface decision is genuinely unsettled — a contract packet whose decisions are already recorded in docs/decisions/ or the plan does not pay for an Architect dispatch. Tester only if risk warrants.

diagnosis.rationale: A reproduced failure whose cause is not obvious. Diagnostician evidences the cause and Builder applies the bounded fix, then the fix is revalidated by the narrowest deterministic command that exercises it — a fix applied before the cause is understood is a guess, and a guess that turns green is the worst outcome available.

$activationComment: When a CONDITIONAL capability actually fires. An optional agent that runs unconditionally is a required agent with worse documentation. `pnpm lanes decide` applies the one condition that is mechanically checkable: a `contract` unit with an open decision gets `architecture` added to its per-packet chain; everything else here is judged by the Coordinator against the listed conditions.

execute: output is long or noisy enough to swamp the calling context
the same command set must be re-run repeatedly
raw verbatim capture must be isolated from an expensive session
validate: a feature packet changed observable behavior after all
a repair landed and the narrow revalidation needs adversarial edge cases, not just the failing command
adversarial-test: a phase gate covering behavior or contract changes
an analyzer, an oracle, or other high-risk logic where a false green kills the product
a repair of a serious false-green defect, where independence from the fixing session matters
integrity-scan: the diff touches test files and product files together
a lane is being integrated (global integration gate)
risk is high, or the change touches a shared write surface
diagnose: a handoff came back BLOCKED with the cause unclear
a reproduced failure survived one bounded repair attempt
architecture: an open decision in scripts/oracle/graph.json names this packet
two readings of the plan lead to materially different work
the packet defines a NEW shared interface no settled decision record (docs/decisions/, the plan, the charter) already covers
retrospective: the same mistake pattern has recurred across at least two completed slices or milestones — never after a single wave, and never mid-implementation

$reviewCadenceComment: Review cadence is DERIVED from the class lifecycle above, not declared twice: `review` in perPacket means per-node review (only `contract` — its mistakes are inherited downstream, so review lands before the next lane builds on it); `review` in perWave means one review at the wave gate over the combined diff; `review` in perPhase means one review at the phase gate; `review` only in conditional means no review unless triggered. CONTEXT.md's rule — validate per wave, review per phase — is the behavior-class row. Finding ownership at any review: review-diff#5 — every finding is tagged `this-node`, a `<node-id>`, or `plan`; only `this-node` blocks the gate; `<node-id>` findings are filed to BACKLOG.md with their trigger. That bound is what keeps a wave or phase review from becoming an unbounded gate.
$responsibilitiesComment: Disjoint by construction. Watchdog and Reviewer are the pair most often collapsed into one call, and collapsing them is how boundary violations get argued about as style. Watchdog answers 'is this allowed'; Reviewer answers 'is this good'. Neither answer substitutes for the other, and `pnpm lanes selftest` asserts the two sets stay disjoint.
$controlPlaneComment: MVP_PLAN_V3.md §9: 'The main Claude Code session is the Coordinator. Do not create a coordinator agent.' Conductor and Integrator are therefore roles the main session holds, not agent files. Creating either as an agent would put a subagent in charge of dispatching subagents, and the session that owns the escalation triggers would no longer be the session that sees the work. Progression itself is decided by `pnpm flow next`, not by prose: LLMs implement and diagnose; code controls progression.
